requirements.evidence: All main requirements are implemented: default map and range fallback (app/Models/Queue.php:24-37), custom map + uniqueness validation (app/Models/Queue.php:60-81), null normalization and save-time enforcement (app/Models/Queue.php:83-96), daily per-prefix next code (app/Models/Ticket.php:38-55), single clock read (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27,34,46,56-57), UpdateQueue parameter/clear/ValidationException (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:20-33,68-69), migrations with backfill and swapped unique index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_064119_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:17-29), factory support (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:34,44-66) and all three docs. Gap: an explicit issue_date is kept even when it disagrees with issued_at (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:44-46), so factory-created rows can violate the 'issue_date must stay aligned with issued_at' rule.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes stay in Actions (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:20-70), authorization remains a Gate check inside the action (:24), the map is deliberately left out of #[Fillable], migrations are reversible and docs/CHANGELOG are updated (docs/business-rules.md:78-81, docs/database-schema.md:101,117,156,164, CHANGELOG.md:25). Deviation from the 'suite must pass' rule: the new test file contains a test that cannot pass (tests/Feature/QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php:142-146).

security.evidence: UpdateQueue still authorizes server-side before any change (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:24); the map is validated for keys (canonical non-negative ints) and values (one A-Z letter) before storage (app/Models/Queue.php:60-81) and is not mass-assignable; no new user-controlled output; no Livewire/Blade changes. Nothing exploitable found.

tests.evidence: Coverage is broad: ranges/defaults, custom map, empty->null, invalid keys/values/duplicates, mass-assignment, per-prefix and per-day sequences, single clock read, legacy A codes, factory allocation, UpdateQueue success/validation/authorization (tests/Feature/QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php:26-210). However tests/Feature/QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php:142 and :146 insert the same malformed code 'N-X' twice for the same queue and day, which violates the unique (queue_id, code, issue_date) index (and the old (queue_id, code) one), so the test errors instead of asserting N002 and the suite is red.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Queue::DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP and validatePriorityPrefixMap from UpdateQueue and the saving hook, and extends the existing nextCode scan rather than adding a new layer; no speculative abstractions. Minor: the factory re-queries the queue with Queue::query()->find($queueId) (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:54) and the map is validated twice on the UpdateQueue path (pre-check plus saving hook).

readability.evidence: Clear PHPDoc and comments (app/Models/Queue.php:19-59, app/Models/Ticket.php:28-37, app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:25-31), small focused methods, descriptive names (prefixForPriority, validatePriorityPrefixMap, defaultPrefixFor), and style matches the surrounding models/actions.

scope.evidence: The diff only touches the models, actions, factory, two migrations, the related tests and the three docs the task names; no UI/totem/refactor or unrelated changes.

issues.explanation: The test creates a ticket with code 'N-X' at line 142 and another 'N-X' for the same queue and same issue_date at line 146; under the unique (queue_id, code, issue_date) index (and even the old (queue_id, code) index) the second insert raises a QueryException, so the file errors instead of asserting N002 and the test suite cannot pass.

issue_date is only derived from issued_at when it is null, so Ticket::factory()->create(['issued_at' => '2026-09-28', 'issue_date' => '2026-09-30']) stores misaligned values, contrary to requirement 5's 'issue_date must stay aligned with issued_at for factory-created rows'.

down() restores unique(queue_id, code) before dropping the column, so it fails whenever the same code was issued on more than one day; the limitation is documented in the comment but means rollback is not reliably reversible after normal use.

review.summary: The change implements per-priority code prefixes, a validated per-queue override map, and daily per-queue/per-prefix sequences with a backfilled issue_date and a new unique index, and it updates the docs. The production logic looks correct and the new tests cover the main and authorization paths, but the suite cannot pass because tests/Feature/QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php inserts the same malformed code twice for the same queue/day, and the factory can still produce issue_date values that disagree with issued_at. Because the change is not mergeable until the red test is fixed, the overall score is 3.
